title: Sato–Tate law for twisted Legendre sums of low-degree coordinates along [k]P
question: Conjecture (Sato–Tate law for twisted Legendre sums along a prime-order EC group). Let E/F_p have #E(F_p)=r prime, P a generator, g in {x, x+a (a in F_p), y}. For c in 1..r-1 let Y_c = p^{-1/2} * sum_{k=0}^{r-1} chi(g([k]P)) e(ck/r). Then |Y_c| <= 2 (+o(1)) for all c, and as p -> infinity (over random such curves) the empirical distribution of Y_c^2 (Y_c real for g = x+a) over c converges to that of (2 cos t)^2 with t Sato–Tate distributed ((2/pi) sin^2 t dt). For g of higher degree (x^2+x+1, xy, x^3+2) the normalized sums are instead approximately Gaussian at these sizes (second moment of |X_c|^2 ≈ 3 for real sums) with max growing within the Weil envelope.
rationale: Sharpened, separately recorded variant of HYP-242da418 after the ECDLP-9 decisive test (two seeds, PI bit-identical reproduction).
assumptions: Toy sizes p <= 1.28e5, 48 curves per predicate per seed.
Sato–Tate identification is by moments (2nd ≈ 2.00, 3rd ≈ 5.0) and KS ≈ 0.012, post-hoc relative to the pre-registered rule.

notes: Experimental finding on toy sizes; no proof; novelty unchecked (likely a known consequence of Deligne/Katz theory).
